source.title: Stručnjakinja za hranu: Debljina nije isključivo pitanje volje!? Donatella Verbanac

summary.title_hr: Stručnjakinja za hranu: Debljina nije isključivo pitanje volje!? Donatella Verbanac
summary.abstract_hr: U epizodi LOOD podcasta voditelj po treći put ugošćuje prof. dr. sc. Donatellu Verbanac. Razgovaraju o tome zašto je Hrvatska prva u Europskoj uniji po udjelu ljudi s viškom kilograma i je li debljina samo pitanje volje i discipline. Gošća objašnjava ulogu epigenetike (na primjeru nizozemske gladi 1944.), hormona štitnjače, inzulina, glukagona i leptina te kako višak masnog tkiva i otpornost na leptin kod pretilih osoba uzrokuju gubitak osjećaja sitosti. Govori se i o GLP-1 lijekovima, koje gošća smatra opravdanom kroničnom terapijom, o demonizaciji farmaceutske industrije, ultraprocesiranoj hrani, fermentiranim namirnicama i jadranskoj prehrani. Razgovor završava porukom da treba prestati kukati, promijeniti stav i preuzeti odgovornost za vlastito zdravlje i 'zdravovječnost'.

speakers.suggested_name: Voditelj (gošća ga jednom oslovljava kao Vinko)
speakers.suggested_name_en: Host (the guest addresses him once as Vinko)

key_points: Gošća ističe da debljina nije stvar samo kalorija ni nedostatka volje. Navodi da smo dugo bili u krivu kad smo osuđivali pretile osobe, a debljina je kao bolest dobila dijagnostičku šifru tek oko 2004. godine.

Na primjeru nizozemske gladi 1944. objašnjava da su potomci žena koje su tada bile trudne imali veću tjelesnu masu zbog epigenetskih promjena koje se mogu prenositi na više generacija. Pita se mogu li slične posljedice imati i oskudne ratne devedesete u Hrvatskoj.
Pretile osobe imaju tri do četiri puta veće razine leptina u krvi, zbog čega receptori postaju rezistentni i osoba gubi osjećaj sitosti. Iz tog začaranog kruga teško je izaći bez pomoći.

GLP-1 lijekovi pomažu da hipotalamus ponovno postane osjetljiv na inzulin i leptin. Prema gošći, najbolje studije pokazuju da je za sada riječ o kroničnoj terapiji, a nakon prestanka uzimanja apetit i kilogrami vjerojatno se vraćaju.

Gošća brani farmaceutsku industriju i navodi primjere inzulina iz 1922. godine i Plivinog azitromicina (Sumamed). Prehrambena industrija, kaže, dobro zna kako optimalnom kombinacijom masti, soli i šećera namamiti ljude.
Procesiranu hranu jedemo brže i do 50% više nego neprocesiranu. Zato preporučuje kuhanje kod kuće, nativne namirnice, fermentiranu hranu poput kiselog kupusa i kefira te jadransku prehranu.
Završna poruka gošće je da se ljudi okrenu sebi, prestanu kukati i čekati da im netko drugi osigura bolji život, nego da promijene stav i uzmu stvari u svoje ruke.
mentioned_organizations: GlaxoSmithKline (u transkriptu zapisano kao 'GLACS u Smithsonianu')
key_topics_en: leptin and the feeling of satiety
key_points_en: The guest emphasizes that obesity is not just a matter of calories or a lack of willpower. She states that we were wrong for a long time when we judged obese people, and obesity received a diagnostic code as a disease only around the year 2004.

Using the example of the Dutch famine of 1944, she explains that the offspring of women who were pregnant at that time had higher body mass due to epigenetic changes that can be transmitted across multiple generations. She wonders whether the scarce war nineties in Croatia could have similar consequences.

Obese individuals have three to four times higher levels of leptin in their blood, which causes receptors to become resistant and the person loses the feeling of satiety. It is difficult to get out of that vicious circle without help.

GLP-1 medications help the hypothalamus become sensitive to insulin and leptin again. According to the guest, the best studies show that for now it is a matter of chronic therapy, and after discontinuation of use, appetite and kilograms likely return.

The guest defends the pharmaceutical industry and cites examples of insulin from the year 1922 and Pliva's azithromycin (Sumamed). The food industry, she says, knows well how to entice people with the optimal combination of fat, salt, and sugar.

We eat processed food faster and up to 50% more than unprocessed food. Therefore, she recommends cooking at home, native ingredients, fermented food such as sauerkraut and kefir, and the Adriatic diet.

The guest's closing message is that people should turn to themselves, stop whining and waiting for someone else to secure a better life for them, but rather change their attitude and take matters into their own hands.

summary.title_en: Food Expert: Obesity Is Not Exclusively a Matter of Willpower!? Donatella Verbanac
summary.abstract_en: In an episode of the LOOD podcast, the host welcomes Prof. Dr. Sc. Donatella Verbanac for the third time. They discuss why Croatia ranks first in the European Union in the proportion of overweight people and whether obesity is merely a question of willpower and discipline. The guest explains the role of epigenetics (using the example of the Dutch famine of 1944), thyroid hormones, insulin, glucagon, and leptin, and how excess fatty tissue and leptin resistance in obese individuals cause the loss of the feeling of satiety. There is also discussion about GLP-1 medications, which the guest considers justified chronic therapy, the demonization of the pharmaceutical industry, ultra-processed food, fermented foods, and the Adriatic diet. The conversation ends with the message that one should stop whining, change one's attitude, and take responsibility for one's own health and 'healthspan'.
